# New renderings — iliad-080 (13.266–360)

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| τὸν καὶ Μηριόνης πρότερος πρὸς μῦθον ἔειπε (13.306, whole-line speech introduction) | "Him also Meriones, first, with a word addressed:" | "Meriones spoke to him first, with these words:" | the Odyssey table’s τὸν καὶ Τηλέμαχος πρότερος πρὸς μῦθον ἔειπεν (16.460) and τὸν καὶ Πείραιος … (17.74), unchanged with the name changed; a departure from iliad-033’s wording for the Tlepolemus line ("to him also Tlepolemus first spoke a word"), because the Odyssey table fixes this formula and the Iliad’s one earlier use is a single line |
| ἀρετὴν οἷός ἐσσι (13.275) | "your excellence, of what sort you are" | "your excellence, what sort of man you are" | "how brave you are", "your courage"; ἀρετή keeps "excellence" (8.535, 9.498) |
| λέγεσθαι · λεγοίμεθα · λεγώμεθα (13.275, 276, 292) | "talk over" · "were picked" · "let us talk over" | "talk of" · "were picked" · "let us stand here talking over" | "be told" (a passive for the middle at 275 and 292), "tell over" (the first draft’s word, a second rendering beside the table’s "talk" for λεγώμεθα, 2.435), "gather" (kept for ἀγείρω); λέγω "pick out" at 276 is told apart from λέγω "talk" in the notes; follows the table’s μηκέτι … λεγώμεθα "let us talk" (2.435) and διελέξατο "talked over" (11.407) |
| ἔνθα μάλιστ’ ἀρετὴ διαείδεται ἀνδρῶν (13.277; διαείδεται rare, sense not certain) | "where most the excellence of men is made plain" | "where the excellence of men is most plainly seen" (+ note: sense not certain) | "is tested", "shows itself through"; follows the table’s ἀρετήν · διαείσεται (8.535) as far as that is settled |
| δειλὸς ἀνήρ · ἄλκιμος (13.278) | "the miserable man" · "the valiant" | "the miserable man" · "the valiant man" | "coward", "craven" (the note says what δειλός means here); keeps the table’s δειλός "miserable" and ἄλκιμος of persons "valiant" |
| κακοῦ · ἀγαθοῦ (of the coward and the brave man, 13.279, 13.284) | "the base man" · "the good man" | "the base man" · "the good man" | "the bad man", "the brave man"; follows the table’s κακός · ἐσθλός (2.365–366), "base" and "good" |
| τρέπεται χρὼς ἄλλυδις ἄλλῃ (13.279) | "the skin turns this way and that" | "the skin … turns this way and that" (+ note: usual explanation is change of colour) | "his colour changes", "turns pale and red" (each decides what the Greek does not say), "now one way, now another" (the first draft’s i, a third wording beside the table’s "this way and that", 11.385); follows the table’s ἄλλυδις ἄλλῃ |
| ἀτρέμας ἧσθαι (13.280) | "to sit motionless" | "to sit motionless" | "to sit still", "quietly"; follows the table’s ἀτρέμας "motionless" (5.523–524) |
| μετοκλάζει (13.281) | "shifts about in a crouch" | "shifts about in a crouch" (+ note: exact posture not clear) | "squats and rises", "shifts from foot to foot" (each decides the posture); μετά "change" + ὀκλάζω "crouch" |
| κραδίη … στέρνοισι πατάσσει (13.282) | "the heart greatly against his breast pounds" | "the heart pounds hard against his breast" | "thumps", "beats wildly", "hammers", "chest" (reserved for στῆθος; στέρνον is "breast", Iliad table 4.528); πατάσσω "strike, pound", κραδίη "heart" as at 1.225 |
| κῆρας ὀϊομένῳ (13.283) | "as he expects death-fates" | "as he expects the fates of death" | "dooms" (the first draft’s word; the table’s κῆρας ἀμύνει 4.11 and κῆρας ἄμυνε 12.402 turn "doom" down), "death", "his fate", "the powers of death"; κήρ "death-fate" (plural), kept apart from κῆρ "heart"; ὀΐομαι "expect" |
| πάταγος ὀδόντων (13.283) | "a chattering of teeth" | "a chattering of teeth" | "clatter", "rattle", "knocking" |
| ἐν δαῒ λυγρῇ (13.286) | "in grievous fray" | "the grievous fray" | "in dire battle", "in baleful strife"; δαΐς "fray", kept apart from μάχη and ὑσμίνη "battle", from ἔρις "strife", from νεῖκος "quarrel" and from πόλεμος "war"; λυγρός "grievous" |
| ταρβεῖ (13.285) · ἀταρβής (13.299) | "is dismayed" · "unafraid" | "is dismayed" · "unafraid" | "is afraid" (turned down at ταρβεῖ οὐδὲ φοβεῖται, 12.46), "fearless"; ταρβέω "be dismayed", as in ταρβήσας "terrified" (6.469) and οὐ ταρβήσας "unafraid" (5.286) |
| ἐσίζηται λόχον ἀνδρῶν (13.285) | "takes his seat in the ambush of men" | "has first taken his seat in the ambush of men" | "settles into an ambush", "lies in wait with other men"; λόχος "ambush" (iliad-003, iliad-025) |
| οὐδέ κεν ἔνθα τεόν γε μένος καὶ χεῖρας ὄνοιτο (13.287) | "nor would one there make light of your might, at least, and your hands" | "no one there could make light of your might or your hands" | "find fault with" (the first draft’s word; Iliad table 4.539 turns it down for ὄνομαι by name), "scorn", "disparage"; ὄνομαι "make light of" (Odyssey 17.378, 5.379); μένος keeps the table’s "might" |
| ὀαριστύν (μετὰ προμάχων ὀαριστύν, 13.291) | "the close converse of the front-fighters" | "the close exchange among the foremost fighters" (+ note: literally "close talk", here close fighting) | "dalliance", "bandying of blows", "parley"; ὀαριστής is "confidant" in the Odyssey (19.179), but the sense here is the fighting; προμάχοι "front-fighters" in `l`, "foremost fighters" in `i` as at 5.681 |
| πονεύμενος (13.288) | "toiling" | "while toiling" | "labouring", "fighting hard"; πονέομαι "toil", as in iliad-025 |
| βέλος (πέσοι βέλος, 13.289) | "the shaft" | "the shaft" | "missile", "arrow" (the Odyssey’s alternatives, which the Iliad table turns down; ὀϊστός keeps "arrow"); follows βέλος "shaft" (4.185, 5.18) |
| νηπύτιοι ὥς (13.292) | "like babes" | "like children" | "like fools", "like infants"; the word is "childish, babyish" |
| ὑπερφιάλως νεμεσήσῃ (13.293) | "beyond measure feel resentment" | "resent it beyond measure" | "overbearingly" (the first draft’s word; "overbearing" is reserved for ὑπερηνορέων, as in iliad-079, and ὑπερφίαλος is "overweening"), "overweeningly" (declined for the adverb in the Odyssey table, 17.481), "take offence", "be proud about it"; ὑπερφιάλως keeps the shipped "beyond measure" (17.481); νεμεσάω keeps "resentment" (iliad-010, iliad-025) |
| βροτολοιγὸς Ἄρης (13.298) | "mortal-ruining Ares" | "Ares, the ruin of mortals" | "man-slaying Ares", "bane of men"; follows the table’s βροτολοιγῷ ἶσος Ἄρηϊ (11.295) |
| Φόβος φίλος υἱός … κρατερὸς καὶ ἀταρβής (13.299) | "Terror, his dear son, strong and unafraid" | "Terror, his dear son, strong and unafraid" | "Rout", "Panic", "Fear" (kept for δέος); Φόβος "Terror" as in 4.440 and 5.739; ἀταρβής "unafraid", "fearless" avoided |
| ταλάφρονά περ πολεμιστήν (13.300) | "even an enduring-minded warrior" | "even a steadfast warrior" | "stout-hearted" (kept for θυμός words), "patient"; ταλάφρων is τλάω + φρήν and is treated as the table’s ταλασίφρων "enduring-minded" / "steadfast" |
| Ἐφύρους · Φλεγύας μεγαλήτορας (13.301–302) | "the Ephyri" · "the great-spirited Phlegyes" | same | "Ephyrians", "Phlegyans"; μεγαλήτωρ keeps "great-spirited" (5.674, 9.109) |
| ἔκλυον ἀμφοτέρων, ἑτέροισι δὲ κῦδος ἔδωκαν (13.303) | "listened to both, but to others gave glory" | "do not listen to both, but give glory to others" (aorists of general statement rendered by the present in `i`) | "pay heed to neither", "heard neither side" (each decides who "the others" are) |
| τοῖοι … ἀγοὶ ἀνδρῶν (13.304) | "Such … leaders of men" | "Such … leaders of men" | "captains of men"; ἀγός "leader" as in Κρητῶν ἀγός (4.265) |
| Δευκαλίδη (13.307) | "Deucalion’s-son" | "Son of Deucalion" | "Deucalid", "Deucalion’s son" unhyphenated in `l`; follows Ἀτρεΐδης / Πριαμίδης |
| πῇ τὰρ μέμονας καταδῦναι ὅμιλον (13.307) | "where then do you intend to go down into the throng" | "where, then, do you intend to go down into the throng" | "plunge into", "enter"; μέμονα "intend" |
| ἐπὶ δεξιόφιν · ἀνὰ μέσσους · ἐπ’ ἀριστερόφιν (13.308–309) | "to the right … through the middle … to the left" | same | "on the right flank", "the centre", "wing" (each makes the army a battle line) |
| οὔ ποθι ἔλπομαι οὕτω δεύεσθαι πολέμοιο (13.309–310; sense of the clause open) | "not anywhere do I expect so to be in want of war" | "I do not expect … to be so short of war anywhere" (+ note: the Greek does not settle the meaning) | "to lack fighters", "to lack fighting spirit", "to be so far from battle" (each decides the open question) |
| νηυσὶ μὲν ἐν μέσσῃσιν ἀμύνειν εἰσί (13.312) | "among the middle ships to defend there are" | "among the ships in the middle there are … to defend" | "to guard the centre of the line", "to hold the middle"; μέσσῃσιν agrees with νηυσί |

| ἀάπτους (χεῖρας, 13.318) | "untouchable" | "irresistible" (+ note: meaning not known; both are traditional guesses) | "invincible" (the first draft’s word, which the table names as turned down; it cited 8.450 in error: the rows are at Odyssey 11.502 and Iliad 11.169), "unconquerable"; follows the table’s ἀάπτους pair "untouchable" / "irresistible" |
